assessments.reasoning: At the exact GCC commit and whole-file digest in scope, lines 9–12 state the FSF-published GPL version choice for “this file”. Lines 22–27 give the inclusion condition and the section 7 designation. These passages directly support both parts of the documentary relationship.

As context, the generated exception record at the verified 3.29.0 data commit confirms the wording of the GPLv3 section 7 sentence. It contains the exception text alone. The GCC header supplies the separate evidence required for the file’s or-later base choice.

challenge.method: Tested a GPL-3.0-only reading by checking the complete base grant against the narrower version reference in the exception’s last sentence and the GPL-3.0 wording in the SPDX record name.
challenge.results: GPL-3.0-only would discard the recipient’s express later-version option. The section 7 sentence identifies the exception’s stated basis. Neither that sentence nor the SPDX name changes the version choice in the file’s grant.

limitations: The finding describes the base choice and exception printed together in this file. It establishes neither project-wide licensing nor the legal effect of the permission under a future GPL edition.
The base edition is explicit in the file. The relationship’s opaque local target ID is registry metadata, and the named documentary sources do not independently resolve that ID.
reasoning: The pinned config.sub header expressly allows “either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.” That language supports the named GPL-3.0-or-later base.
